newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas leader pledges to continue political work.
newsitem.headline: Hamas leader pledges to continue political work.

text.p: Musa Abu Marzook, political leader of the militant Palestinian movement Hamas, pledged on Tuesday to continue to work for the organisation after his release from nearly two years detention in a New York jail.
"I will continue in political activities. Naturally the motives that made me stand with the hopes and aspirations of my people still exist," Abu Marzook told a news conference at his home in Amman.
"I have still a lot to do to serve my people and help them achieve their aspirations," a relaxed Abu Marzook said.

Abu Marzook, born in Gaza in 1951, thanked Jordan's King Hussein for welcoming him back to Jordan. He said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had called his family to congratulate them on his release.

Hamas opposes Arafat's self-rule deal with Israel as a sell-out and its military wing has launched a series of attacks in recent years in which scores of Israelis have died. Israel said Abu Marzook controlled the leadership of the military wing and was involved in the attacks.
But Abu Marzook, expelled from Jordan in 1995 under pressure from Washington, Israel and the Palestinians, has denied any role in violence.
